“The effects of the coronavirus will weigh on economic activity in the near term and pose risks to the economic outlook,” but the policy response is forceful and aligned with macro-finance research. Consistent with the credit-channel/financial-accelerator literature (e.g., Bernanke–Gertler; Gertler & Gilchrist), the rate cut to the effective lower bound, large-scale purchases of Treasuries and MBS, expanded repos, the discount window, and dollar swap lines are designed to lower external finance premia and stabilize investment and employment. With market-based inflation compensation falling, the use of QE and strong forward guidance is also supported by liquidity-trap and inflation-forecast-targeting work (Svensson; Woodford; Calvo price stickiness), helping anchor expectations around the symmetric 2% goal. A state-contingent commitment in the face of real-time data uncertainty (Orphanides) further aligns with best-practice monetary policy. Overall tone: negative due to the shock and outlook risks, partially offset by credible, literature-consistent policy support.
